notes: Burrow (Hydrogen/Shopify-Oxygen headless). Direct HTTP fetch throughout, no blocking, robots.txt clean. Site's own nav exposes a genuine parent/child taxonomy: home-page + mega-menu link labelled 'Warehouse Sale' / 'Up to 70% off Warehouse' -> /collections/clearance (H1 'Warehouse', meta 'Save on quality furniture with warehouse pricing... while supplies last', breadcrumb Home>Bestsellers>Warehouse[sic on breadcrumb 3rd segment likely a CMS quirk]), with 3 nav-linked children by breadcrumb 'Warehouse Sale > {Seating|Outdoor|Storage}': /collections/clearance-seating, /collections/clearance-outdoor, /collections/clearance-storage. Verified via Playwright (unique /products/ base handles in <main>, Load-more exhausted) that parent and children are genuinely DIFFERENT product sets, not aliases: parent(40) vs clearance-seating(40) share only 24/40 (16 unique each side); parent(40) vs clearance-outdoor(50) share only 6/50 -- so each is a distinct real listing, kept as separate rows per brief. Sitemap also lists /collections/clearance-dining, /collections/clearance-rugs, /collections/clearance-pillows and /collections/labor-day-clearance, none linked from current nav. The first three (dining/rugs/pillows) rendered 0 products (confirmed empty via main-grid DOM count) -- dropped per 'drop zero-product listings' rule, not emitted as rows. /collections/labor-day-clearance DOES have live products (42, verified same DOM method) and its title/breadcrumb literally say 'Labor Day Clearance', so it is recorded -- but flagged ambiguous: its breadcrumb is flat (Home>Labor Day Clearance, NOT nested under 'Warehouse Sale' like the 3 confirmed children), the homepage's own banner calls the current event a 'Labor Day SALE' (temporary/seasonal), and its product mix (mostly Dunes teak outdoor + Relay outdoor sectionals, 35 of 42 items) only overlaps 7/42 with the Warehouse clearance parent -- consistent with a time-limited end-of-summer outdoor promotional sale rather than permanent outlet/discontinued stock, though the literal 'Clearance' naming argues the other way. Checked for other clearance/outlet/final-sale/last-chance wording via full sitemap grep (156 handles) and homepage nav dump -- no other candidates found.
